abstract: Music-understanding benchmarks should identify both the evidence available to a model and the operations a correct answer requires. We introduce HMU-Bench, a bilingual benchmark with notation and audio components. ABC Q&A contains 1,029 Chinese-English question pairs across six musical domains, labeled as extraction, single-step inference, or multi-step inference. Audio Q&A contains 460 question pairs on 92 recordings, spanning five scope-difficulty configurations. All music is Suno-generated, and questions and references are human-reviewed. Reference-based evaluation of seven omni models yields high notation scores for the strongest systems, but no model averages above 1.4 on the 0-4 audio scale. Notation and audio rankings show little correlation. A transposition case study also reveals octave errors missed by LLM grading. These findings motivate separate modality reporting and event-level checks for symbolic outputs. Data, annotations, evaluator prompts, and graded responses will be released at https://github.com/stepaudiollm/hmu-bench.

oneSentenceThesis: HMU-Bench 用 1029 对乐谱问答和 460 对音频问答考查同一批全模态模型，最强系统乐谱得分接近 3.9 而音频最高仅 1.33，且两类排名几乎无关，局部困难音频与移调八度错误进一步暴露了评分与定位短板。
originalTitle: HMU-Bench: Hierarchical Music Understanding Benchmark for Omni Models
